Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines, if any.

Company acknowledges and is committed to conduct its business in a sustainable and responsible manner. The purpose and the core values for the company are closely interlinked with the concept of ESG. Company is committed to ESG strategy and targets set by the Company with a roadmap in place. Major Targets are: a) Diversity, inclusion and equal opportunity b) To encourage and to make efficient use of resources such as less paper consumption in our offices c) For necessary car trips, use small, energy-efficient electric vehicles d) Identify and continuously aim towards improvement in effective resource (waste / energy) management within its own operations e) Climate Risk Framework or Management system shall be a focus area.
Performance of the entity against the specific commitments, goals and targets along-with reasons in case the same are not met.

a) Company aims to be an equal opportunity employer. In FY 2024-25, our gender diversity improved with women representing 24% of our workforce, and we hired 74 differently abled employees. b) Company is working towards zero paper consumption through tracking, reducing, and eliminating paper usage. Regular awareness e-mailers are issued, and monitoring is ongoing. c) Electric Vehicle Trips are used for necessary car trips. d) Company enhances energy efficiency by using energy-efficient LED lighting, 3-star or higher- rated air conditioning units, and eliminating single-use plastic. e) As a Health insurance company, company has limited exposure to climate impacts. Risks primarily arise from exposure to physical impacts on owned assets and clients affected by climate change.

% of your plants and offices that were assessed (by entity or statutory authorities or third parties)

During the year, we assessed 100% of our offices for compliance with the provisions of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 and the Rules framed thereunder. The assessment process involved (a) verifying the constitution of a duly constituted Internal Committee for each office, (b) ensuring that the POSH policy has been appropriately disseminated among all employees, (c) confirming that posters/ information against sexual harassment have been displayed in conspicuous areas within the workplace, and (d) evaluating whether all employees have undergone training to raise awareness of their rights and responsibilities under the POSH framework.
% of value chain partners (by value of business done with such partners) that were assessed

We do not conduct a due diligence or assessment of Value Chain partners. We cover this aspect through contractual clauses and obligations built into our agreements. To ensure compliance, we have integrated specific measures into our engagement processes with suppliers, vendors, and contractors. These measures include details w.r.t. vendors complying with all laws, by-laws, ordinances, circulars, directions, rules and regulations as may be applicable which includes adherence to POSH Act as well. We have further obligated them to abide by ILO (International Labour Organization) principles, which include safety and security of women. Our organization is committed to upholding the principles of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 and Rules, 2013 across our entire value chain.

The Company recognizes that its purpose and core values are closely aligned with responsible and sustainable business conduct. In line with this, it has defined a clear ESG direction supported by a structured roadmap and identified priority focus areas, including: • Advancing diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunity across the organization • Reducing paper consumption and improving overall resource efficiency in office operations • Promoting the use of smaller, fuel-efficient vehicles for official travel • Strengthening waste management and energy efficiency practices within operations • Progressively developing a climate risk management framework as a key area of focus In parallel, the Company’s Board-approved CSR Policy reinforces its commitment to social impact, with interventions across areas such as: • Health, hygiene, and sanitation • Nutrition and livelihood support • Health insurance awareness • Education and disaster relief initiatives Together, these efforts demonstrate the Company’s broader commitment to inclusive growth, sustainability, and responsible business practices.

The Company continues to make steady progress across its identified ESG priorities, with a strong focus on embedding sustainability within its operations and culture. Notably, NBHI operates as a 100% paperless company, reflecting its commitment to resource efficiency and environmental responsibility. Key initiatives undertaken during the year include: • Improvement in gender diversity, with women representing 25% of the workforce, alongside targeted efforts to enhance inclusion through hiring of differently abled individuals • Continued focus on paper reduction through process digitization, monitoring, and awareness initiatives • Adoption of electric vehicle-based travel for official purposes where feasible • Implementation of energy-efficiency measures, including use of LED lighting and higher-rated air-conditioning systems • Elimination of single-use plastics across operations In parallel, the Company’s Board-approved CSR Policy supports its broader social impact agenda, with structured oversight and implementation across the following focus areas: • Health, hygiene, and sanitation • Nutrition and livelihood initiatives • Health insurance awareness • Education and disaster relief These initiatives are supported by defined governance, monitoring, and accountability mechanisms, reinforcing the Company’s commitment to responsible business practices and inclusive growth.
Statement by director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets, and achievements

At Niva Bupa, responsible business conduct is an integral part of our strategy and long-term value creation. As a health insurance company, our primary responsibility is to improve access to quality healthcare while maintaining the highest standards of governance, ethics, customer trust, and stakeholder engagement. During the year, we continued to strengthen our ESG framework through enhanced governance oversight, employee well-being initiatives, diversity and inclusion programs, customer-centric digital solutions, and responsible environmental practices across our operations. We also progressed in areas such as 100% reduction in paper consumption, energy-efficient infrastructure, and increased awareness of sustainability practices among employees through our ESG Newsletters. While the Company has limited direct environmental impact compared with manufacturing industries, we recognize the growing implications of climate-related risks on communities, healthcare systems, and our stakeholders. Accordingly, we remain focused on strengthening our ESG risk management approach and integrating sustainability considerations into our business processes. Our Risk Register includes ESG, Climate Change, and CSR Risk. The organization achieved a Trust Index score of 84, maintaining a consistently strong level of employee trust even as participation expanded significantly, with nearly 1,300 additional employees taking part in the survey this year. This year, the organization achieved its first-ever 5/5 Culture Audit rating, improving from 3/5 two years ago to 4/5 last year. These results have contributed to Niva Bupa being recognized as a Great Place to Work® Certified organization, as well as being ranked among the Top 25 Best Workplaces in BFSI and the Top 50 Best Workplaces in Health & Wellness. Going forward, we will continue to focus on responsible growth, customer trust, employee development, operational efficiency, and measurable ESG outcomes aligned with applicable regulatory expectations and stakeholder interests. We remain committed to conducting business responsibly and creating sustainable value for all stakeholders.

Yes. The Company has a formal Employee Grievance Redressal Mechanism to enable employees to raise and resolve workplace-related concerns in a timely, fair and confidential manner. Employees can submit grievances through multiple channels, including the digital Employee Helpdesk (ticket- based system), dedicated email IDs for payroll-related queries, the Exit Helpdesk for exiting employees, and direct escalation to the HR Business Partner (HRBP). Grievances are assigned to the relevant SPOC for resolution within defined timelines, with an escalation matrix in place for unresolved cases. The mechanism ensures confidential handling of grievances and protection against retaliation, promoting a transparent and respectful work environment.
